analysis:
The patch to coordinator/api/dispatch.go only changes first-content timing in the dispatch state machine. It adds fallbackDeadline and promptDeadlineForWork fields, replaces global deadline helpers with per-pending-request variants (firstTokenWaitFor, firstTokenSpeculativeWaitFor, canExtendPreambleLivenessFor, firstContentDurationFor, firstTokenRemainingFor), re-arms expired timers after held preamble chunks, and adds expireBoundFirstContentRacer. It also moves configureFirstContentReservation after FirstContentDeadline is set (around line 1419) and uses firstTokenWriteContextForPending for the write context (around line 1706).

I found no change to authentication, App Attest or legacy serving authorization, encryption (sealing/E2E), billing settlement, or data exposure. The final authorization check at write handoff is untouched in the visible hunks. Availability is the only relevant property (T-010, T-057 adjacent), and the visible hunks bound waits more tightly rather than loosening them.

Coverage limits: the new helper bodies (in other files such as first_content_retry.go), the promptDeadlineForWork definition, and expireBoundFirstContentRacer were not supplied. A next pass should check that rearmExpiredFirstContentTimer and rearmExpiredFirstContentRaceTimer cannot extend the request-absolute first-token budget indefinitely. A provider-controlled stream of preamble chunks could otherwise keep rearming the timer and hold a reserved provider or GPU slot. A pass should also check that the unsupplied helpers cannot let a timeout skip the provider-fault attribution in providerAttemptAttributableStall, which now receives per-request durations. The review is limited to the supplied hunks.
